slot.brief: A wire is stretched to double its length at constant volume; find the factor by which resistance changes.

stem: A uniform metal wire is drawn through rollers until its length becomes twice its original length. Assuming its volume and resistivity remain unchanged, by what factor does its resistance change?

verdicts.working: With constant volume, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area. Since $R=\rho L/A$ and resistivity is unchanged, the resistance becomes $2/(1/2)=4$ times its original value.

working:
$V=AL=\text{constant}\Rightarrow A'=A/2$
$R'=\dfrac{\rho(2L)}{A/2}=4\dfrac{\rho L}{A}=4R$

Independent check: With constant volume, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area. Since $R=\rho L/A$ and resistivity is unchanged, the resistance becomes $2/(1/2)=4$ times its original value.
solution:
With constant volume, $AL=A'L'$, so doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area: $A'=A/2$.
$$\frac{R'}{R}=\frac{\rho(2L)/(A/2)}{\rho L/A}=4$$
